full_judgment:
Md. Ansar Ali J: This Death Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the confirmation of the death sentence passed on the condemned prisoner Md. Musa alias Mussaiya alias Shafir Bap and the connected Jail Appeal No. 1407 of 1991 and the Criminal Appeal No. 413 of 1991 by the said condemned prisoner together with the Criminal Appeal No. 826 of 1991 by convict Md. Anowar Miah alias Anowarjja alias Baghiya, son of Abdul Latif arise out of the same judgment and order dated 30.3.1991 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Sessions Trial Case No. 41 of 1988 convicting appellant Md. Musa alias Musaiya alias Shapir Bap, appellant Anowar Miah alias Baghiya and accused Nurul Islam alias Islam alias Nurul Haq and accused Ahmedul Haq under section 396 of the Penal Code and sentencing accused Md. Musa alias Musaiya alias Shapir Bap to death by hanging by the neck till his death and three others namely, Nurul Islam, Ahmedul Haque and Anowar Miah alias Baghaiya to imprisonment for life and acquitted the rest of the accused persons namely, Nurul Islam, son of Babuilya and absconding accused Abdul Mannan, Nurul, Amin, Anowar Mia, Ezahar Mia and Shah Alam. The appeals and the reference are heard together and being disposed of by the following one judgment.

2. The prosecution case, in short, as stated in the Ejahar is that the informant Promode Barua lives in Chittagong City with members of his family and earns his livelihood as Motor Driver, his paternal homestead is situated at Barua Para at village Abdullahpur within PS Fatickchari. On 20-4-1985 he received an information that a dacoity was committed in his paternal homestead in the night following 19-4-1986. He rushed to the place of occurrence house and gathered information from his father, mother and Bhabis and came to know about the occurrence and then filed the ejahar to the Police Officer present at the place of occurrence at about 13.15 hours on 20-4-1985; that on the fateful night the inmates of the 1-use namely, his father, mother and two brothers the victims Dilip and Pintu and Bhabis fell asleep after taking meal in their west bhiti hut. Brothers of the informant Dilip and Pintu slept in the southern room of the dwelling house. At about 3-00 AM inmates of the house were awakened by sound of knocking at the door; then 4/5 dacoits broke open the door and entered into the room and started beating Dilip and Pintu who out of fear entered into the contiguous northern room through the intervening door. The dacoits followed them into the northern room and there was a tussle between the dacoits and the brothers of the informant in that room. At one stage one of the dacoits shouted asking other dacoits to kill the inmates of the house and instantaneously one of the dacoits opened fire with the firearms in his hand upon victim Dilip. Another dacoit gave blow with a dagger at the abdomen of victim Pintu causing serious injuries; thereafter the dacoits left the place after looting away the articles noted in the petition namely, 4 golden rings, wrist watch and some cash money worth Taka 4, 750/00. There were 6/7 other dacoits on guard outside the house at the time of occurrence. The victim Dilip died instantaneously and Pintu was seriously injured both in the northern room of the house. The dacoits were equipped with gun, lathi, torchlight, etc. Few of the dacoits also used masks and some of them wore half pants and some lungi with malkocha and their age was between 15-20 years and that the dacoity took place for more than 10/15 minutes, that inmates of the house had seen the dacoits at the time of dacoity and they would be able to recognise the dacoits who were without masks if produced before them. After the departure of the dacoits from the place of occurrence the mother, father and bhabics of the informant made hue and cry when neighbouring people came and saw the occurrence. They had seen the deceased, victim Dilip and the seriously injured victim Pintu who was sent to Chittagong Medical College Hospital for urgent treatment. The dead body of the victim Dilip was lying in the house at the time of lodging the ejahar. Pintu was in hospital where he died of the injuries. PW 13 Enam Ahmed Chowdhury the Police Officer was out from the Thana on the basis of a GD entry No. 614 dated 20-4-1984. On the way he heard about the occurrence and went to the place of occurrence house and received the First Information from the PW 1 Promode Barua, brother of the deceased victim at 13.15 hours on the same day; he thereafter sent the said information to the Fatickchari Police Station through a constable and the said information was recorded in a regular First In-irmation Report form in the Thana on the same day at 21.45 hours by one Abul Hosan, Daroga of Fatikchari Police Station and accordingly, Fatikchari PS Case No. 4(4)85 was started under section 396 of the Penal Code. PW 13 Enam Ahmed Chowdhury took up the investigation of the case. He seized some alamats at the place of occurrence, held inquest on the dead-body of the victim Dilip in presence of witnesses and thereafter sent the dead-body to the Chittagong Hospital for post mortem examination and report. He prepared the sketch map of the place of occurrence, examined some witnesses under section 161 CrPC and meanwhile victim Pintu died in the hospital and his Surat-hal Report was also prepared there and thereafter his post mortem examination was held and a report was made by the doctor.

3. The first investigating officer PW 13 Enam Ahmed Chowdhury on his transfer handed over the investigation of the case to PW 17 Abdul Hamid, Officer-in-Charge of the PS on 5-7-1985. He thereafter visited the place of occurrence on 16-7-1985, seized some more alamats, examined more witnesses under section 161 CrPC, prepared a seizure list and during investigation according to his deposition arrested accused Md. Musa @ Musaiya on 2-9-1985 and took steps for showing other 4 accused namely, Md. Anowar @ Baghaiya, son of Abdul Latif, Mahmudul @ Ahmedul Hoque, son of Muklesur Rahman, Nurul Islam @ Islam @ Nurul Huq son of Noor Mohamad and Nurul Islam @ Bubuillya son of late Nuru Mistry as arrested. Thereafter he sought for permission to hold TI parade of the suspected accused persons and he also sought remand for some of them for 5 days which was allowed and the period of remand being over he produced some of the accused namely Musa @ Musaiya, Ahmedul Haque and Md. Anowar @ Baghaiya before the Magistrate PW 14 Tofazzal Ahmed i.e. the local Upazila Magistrate who recorded a plain paper confessional statement of the accused and then sent them back to the custody of the officer-in charge of the police station and the TI parade of the suspects was held on 24-11-85 in the Chittagong Jail in presence of PW 15 Md. Ahmed Hossain a Magistrate. From the TI Paradesheet it appears that 8 suspects were placed in the TI parade and one Sultan Azizul Haque the Jailor was witness of the parade but he has not been examined as a witness and according to the TI Parade report PW 4 Ledu Banu, a wife of Kiron Chandra Barua identified Nurul Islam, PW Gita Rani Barua identified Musa @ Musaiya and PW 3 Barua also identified Md. Musa @ Musaiya. However on receipt of the post mortem report of the victims and after conclusion of the investigation of the case PW 17 submitted charge-sheet on 8-2-86 as against 8 accused persons including these 2 convicts under section 396 of the Penal Code. The case was thereafter transmitted to the Court of the learned Sessions Judge for trial who was pleased to receive the case records and register the same and thereafter transferred the case to the court of the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong for trial.

4. The learned Assistant Judge framed charge as against 10 accused persons under section 396 of the Penal Code of whom accused Abdul Manrtan alias Manaiya, Nurul Amin alias Aminaiya, Anowar Miah alias Anowarjjaiya, Ejahar Mcah and Shah Alam alias Shali alias Manna were absconding and the necessary legal formalities were observed for their trial in absentia.

5. The accused’s who were present in court pleaded not guilty to the charge and claimed to be tried. The prosecution produced in all 17 PWs in Court out of whom PW 1, brother of the victim, is the informant, PW 2 Shudatta Ramjan Barua is a member of the local Union Council and a neighbour of the informant, Shanu Barua is the bhabi of the informant, PW 4 Ledu Barua is the mother of the informant and PW 5 Gita Rani Barua is another bhabi of the informant. The 3 PWs. namely, PWs 3, 4 and 5 are alleged to be the inmates of the house and the eye-witnesses of the occurrence, PW 6 Abul Kashem ASI of Police made the inquest on the dead-body of victim Pintu in the hospital and sent the dead-body of the said victim to the morgue for post mortem examination and by Chalan Ext. 3. PW 7 is constable Shamsul Haque who brought the dead body of the victim Dilip in the hospital. PW 8 is Babul Chandra Barua. PW 9 is Amal Kanti Barua, PW 10 is Sudharshan Barua. PW 11 is Provath Kushum Barua, and PW 12 is Abinash Chandra Barua who is alleged to have come to the place of occurrence after the occurrence but they were all tendered and not cross-examined by the defence. Only PW 10 Sudharshan Barua stated in cross examination that at 2/2.30 AM he went to the place of occurrence but did not see any dacoit. PW 13 is the first investigating officer as already stated. PW 14 Tofazzal Ahmed is the UNO and Magistrate who recorded the confessional statements of accused Ahammadul Hoque and Md. Anowar alias Bagiya under section 164 CrPC and PW 15 is another Magistrate who is alleged to have held the TI parade for identification of the suspected accused’s on 14-11-85. PW 16 Mr. Hashanuzzaman is the doctor who held the post mortem examination on the dead body of the 2 victims Dilip and Pintu and gave his report and PW 17 is the 2nd investigating officer who ultimately submitted the charge sheet in this case.

6. The defence did not examine any witness and from the trend of the cross-examination of the PWs the defence plea appears to be that they have been falsely implicated in this case out of suspicion and that the real culprits of the case could not be caught and brought for trial and that the alleged confessions of accused Ahammadul Huq and Md. Anowar @ Babullya arc not true and voluntary and that the same have not been recorded in accordance with the law after proper compliance of the provisions of sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Further defence is that the alleged TI Parade has not been held in accordance with law and the so-called identification is false and not correct and the same was done illegally at the showing of some policemen present there and, as such, it was not independent, legal and proper. The learned Additional Sessions Judge however in consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record was pleased to find the accused namely, Md. Musa alias Musaiya @ Shapir Bap, Nurul Islam @ Islam @ Nurul Hoque son of Noor Ahmed, Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya and Ahmedul Hoque guilty under section 396 of the Penal Code and sentenced them thereunder as stated above but acquitted the rest of the accused persons by the impugned judgment and order out of which this death reference for confirming the death sentence of condemned prisoner Md. Musa @ Musaiya @ Shapir Bap and his two appeals being Jail Appeal No. 1407 of 1991 and Criminal Appeal No. 413/1991 have come before us for consideration as stated above.

7. Mr. Shaikh Zulfiqar Bulbul Chowdhury with Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan the learned Advocates appeared for the condemned prisoner and also for another co-accused Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya and Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr. AQM Rashid appeared for the State in support of the reference and for the State.

8. Mr. Zulfiqar Bulbul Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, took us through entire paper book including the supplementary paper book containing the First Information Report the charge, the evidence of the PWs, the Post Mortem Report, the 342 statements, the confessional statement, the seizure list, sketch map, TI Parade report, etc, and the other materials on record including the impugned judgment and order. He thereafter seriously opposed the reference and assailed the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence as against these 2 appellants on various grounds. His first contention is, that the ingredients of the charge under section 396 PC as framed against the appellants have not been fully established and vis-a-vis the place, time and the manner of occurrence by reliable and sufficient evidence by the prosecution. His next material contention is, that the prosecution has totally failed to identify the real culprits of the alleged occurrence. Admittedly none of the 3 alleged eye-witnesses PWs 3, 4 and 5 could recognise and name the dacoits. The prosecution case is that some of the dacoits wore mask on their faces and some did not have any mask and they would be able to recognize those dacoits who were unmasked and that is why none of the accused was named in the First Information Report and for the purpose of recognition accordingly a TI parade was subsequently held in presence of a Magistrate and further, according to the prosecution, PW 4 Ladu Barua mother of the victim recognised one Nurul Islam and PW 3 Sanu Barua recognised appellant Musa @ Musaiya and also PW 5 Gita Rani Barua recognised said accused Musa @ Musaiya in the TI Parade but it is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that admittedly the night was very dark and hence it was difficult for the PWs to recognise the real culprits. It is further contended on behalf of the appellants that there were material contradictions in the depositions of the so-called eye-witnesses with regard to the identification of these appellants and the so-called TI parade was not held in time and in accordance with the law and the settled practice and the procedure. Rather it was held long after the arrest of the appellants without any cogent reason and further police was present at the scene of the alleged TI Parade to assist the witnesses to identify the suspects as participants in the crime which was not legally permissible and, as such, relying on such doubtful and materially defective recognition of the accused appellant Musa @ Musaiya, no conviction could be legally given to him and hence his conviction and sentence cannot be sustained in law. The next contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant is that the alleged confession of accused appellant Md. Anowar is no confession in the eye of law and the same is not true or voluntary inasmuch as it was not recorded in a regular printed form and the mandatory provisions of section 164(3) and section 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have not been fully complied with in recording the alleged confession and further, the said alleged confession has also not been brought to the notice of the accused appellant Md.Anowar Baghiya at the time of his statement under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant to the effect that there is no iota of evidence as against Md. Anowar Bagaiya implicating him in any way in the commission of the alleged dacoity and except his so-called confessional statement as recorded in the paper marked Ext. 9A. Therefore the learned Advocate for the appellants argued that in fact it is a case of no evidence against these appellants and they have been most illegally and improperly convicted and sentenced and hence the appeals should be allowed and the impugned conviction and sentence of the appellants should accordingly be set aside and the criminal reference in respect of the condemned prisoner Musa CI) Musaiya be rejected and with the appellants be acquitted of the charge levelled against them.

9. Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, submits that the prosecution has been able to prove its case of dacoity with murder vis-a-vis the place, time and the manner of occurrence by sufficient and reliable evidence. He further submits that PWs 3-5 are the most natural and reliable eye-witnesses and they have proved the occurrence. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that during the dacoity two victims namely, Dilip and Pintu were done to death. So far victim Dilip is concerned he died instantaneously and the other victim Pintu received stabbing injury on his abdomen during the occurrence by one of the dacoits and as a result he died in the hospital on the following day. Thus it is a clear case of dacoity with murder and the same has been sufficiently proved by oral evidences by other witnesses and the medical reports and evidence of the Dr. PW 16. Further contention of the learned Deputy Attorney-General as regards the recognition of the accused is that they have been seen at the time of occurrence and recognised at the TI parade held subsequently within the jail. The condemned prisoner Musa has been recognised by the eye-witnesses and in spite of some irregularities as contended by the other side in holding the TI parade, the same can be relied upon in view of the presumption that arises under section 11 of the Evidence Act. Hence the recognition based in the TI parade has been rightly given due weight by the trial Court. As regards the confessional statement of accused Md. Anowar Bagaiya, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that it is true that the confessional statement was recorded on a plain paper but for that it cannot be said the confessional statement is not voluntary and there may be some irregularities in recording the confession but those cannot be deemed to be fatal after examination of the recording Magistrate as a witness in this case.

10. Now before entering into the discussion on the submissions of the learned Advocates we propose to go into the evidence on record. Finally, let us see evidence of the Doctor PW 16 who held the Post Mortem examination on the dead bodies of the victims. He stated in evidence that while he was the professor of Forensic Medicine in Chittagong Medical College, he held the Post Mortem Examination on the dead body of victim Dilip Barua on 21-4-1985 and recorded the following injuries: (1) One rounded hole on the right side of the abdomen 1" right from the mid line. (2) One lacerated wound 1/4" X 1/4" on the abdomen. On dissection he found stomach and intestine ruptured. In his opinion, death of the victim was due to shock and hemorrhage caused by the above mentioned injuries. The injuries were caused by bullets fired from firearm which were antemortem and homicidal in nature.

11. He also held post mortem examination on the dead body of deceased victim Pintu on the same day and found the following injuries: (1) One penetrating wound 2"X1" on the right side of the abdomen from which intestine came out.

12. On dissection he found one penetrating wound 1" X 1/4" on the ascending colon. In his opinion the death of the victim was due to haemorrhage and shock caused by above mentioned injuries by sharp cutting pointed weapon which were antemortem and homicidal in nature.

13. In cross-examination he denied a suggestion with regard to the injury on the body of victim Dilip that it was not a bullet injury. In respect of victim Pintu he stated that in his stomach some fluid was found but that was not medically tested. He denied a suggestion that he submitted an perfunctory post mortem report.

14. Now PW 1 Promod Barua is the informant in the case. He is not an eye-witness of the occurrence and he was staying at Chittagong and after hearing about the occurrence from one of his relations he came to the place of occurrence house at about 8-00 AM on 20-4-85 and and after consulting with his father, mother, bhabis and other inmates he lodged the First Information Report on the spot to the Police. He stated that on the fateful night after taking meal the inmates of the house went to bed in the west bhiti gudam ghar. Victim Pintu and Dilip were sleeping in the southern room. At about 3-00 AM 10-12 dacoits came to the place of occurrence house and 4/5 of them broke open the door and entered into the room wherein there was scuffling between the victims and the dacoits and at that moment a dacoit fired at Dilip when he fell down and instantly died and other dacoits gave stabbing blows on the abdomen of the victim, Pintu who also fell down. Thereafter the dacoits decamped with cash and other articles worth Taka 4,750.00. Pintu was taken to the CMCH where he succumbed to his injuries. This witness stated that the dacoits had dagger, lathi, gun and torch light and they were wearing half pant and lungis with malkocha, faces of some of them were covered by cloth and the dacoity took place for about 10/15 minutes and the dacoits also assaulted his mother and bhabi. He further stated that his father, mother and bhabies would be able to recognise the dacoits if brought before them. He further stated that at their hue and cry, the neighbours Abinash Barua, Sudatta Barua, Babul Barua, Sudhan Barua, Provat Kusum and many others came to the place of occurrence house and to them his mother and bhabies narrated the occurrence and thereafter he lodged the First Information Report marked as Ext. 4 and his signature Ext. 1/1. In cross examination he stated that he was at Chittagong on the day of occurrence and whatever he stated was hearsay. He stated that he reached his house at 8-00 AM and that the distance of Chittagong Town from his house would be 22 miles. He stated that his cousin brother Parulla gave him information and that he at 11-30 /12-00 AM lodged the First Information Report and thereafter Police came and stayed in their house for about 2 hours. He stated that the Police seized the broken door and some blood stained earth.

15. PW 2 is Sudatta Ranjan Barua. He was the member of the Abdullapur Union Council. His house is at a distance of 300 yards in the east from place of occurrence house. He stated that on 19-4-85 in the night at about 3-00 AM hearing sound of gunshot he woke up from sleep and came out from his house and while going towards the place of occurrence house he saw some persons running away towards the south western side of the place of occurrence house. He stated that going to the place of occurrence house he found that Dilip was lying dead with bullet injury and Pintu was lying injured due to stabbing by dagger. He also found some neighbours and other inmates of the house. He also found Gita Barua, Shenu Barua, Ledu Barua and they all told him that about 10/12 dacoits had entered into the room of Dilip and Pintu and assaulted them. He further stated that victim Dilip caught hold of a dacoit and Pintu gave a dagger blow on one of the dacoits and thereafter Dilip was fired at by one of the dacoits and he fell down and died at once. Pintu was thereafter given a dagger blow and he sustained grievous injury and subsequently he was admitted in CMCH but there he died on the following day. He stated that the dacoit dacamped with gold, money and other articles. He stated that the dacoits were wearing lungis, half pants, ganjis, etc. and some of the dacoits were without any shirt or ganji. Some of the inmates of the house recognised the faces of the dacoits and they would be able to identify the dacoits if they could be seen again. He stated that he signed the surathal report of the victim and that police seized some alamats namely empties of bullets, blood stained clothes, blood stained earth, cover of SIR's cartridges, bark of a tree, the broken wood of the door as alamats made a seizure list Ext. 2 and his signature on the same is Ext. 2/1. In cross-examination he stated that he went to the place of occurrence house at about 3-3/15-00 AM but he did not see the father of the informant as he had fled away. He stated that he remained there till morning and then again came to the place of occurrence house at 1/1.30 when the police came. He further stated that the informant came and reached the place of occurrence house when the police came. He stated that the police came to the place of occurrence on receipt of the information by telephone but he did not tell who gave such information by telephone. He stated that the dead-body of the victim Dilip was lying on the ground and was not covered by anything. He stated that the father of the informant came to the house when police came. He stated that his house and the house of the informant was intervened by 20/22 houses. He stated that about 100/150 persons assembled at place of occurrence. He stated that Dilip and Pintu were in the same room. He denied a suggestion that he was giving false evidence because of his relationship with the informant.

16. PW 3 Shanu Barua is one of bhabies of the informant as well as of the victims. She stated that about 3-00 AM the dacoits broke open the door of the house of her father-in-law and entered into the same and she was at that time sleeping. She stated that Dilip Barua and Pintu had scuffling with the dacoits and when dacoits entered into her room then scuffling started and Pintu gave a blow on one of the dacoits and then one of the dacoits fired at Dilip when he fell down and died instantaneously and the dacoit also gave stabbing blow on the abdomen of the victim Pintu and that they were 12/13 in number. They took away a golden ring from the hand of the victim Pintu a sicho wrist watch from beneath the pillow of the victims and a cash of Taka 200.00, that she recognised the dacoits in the focus of their torch light. She stated that she recognised the dacoit namely, Md. Musa @ Musaiya. She stated that in her room, Gita Rani and her mother-in- law Ledu Barua were also present and Gita Rani could recognise accused Musa @ Musaiya, her mother-in-law Ledu Barua could recognise accused Nurul Islam @ Nurul Huq. She stated that on their hue and cry, people gathered in their house and she narrated the occurrence to them and she stated that she would be able to recognise the accused if they were produced before her. Subsequently the Police took her along with Gita Rani and her mother-in-law to the jail where she recognised the accused’s. She stated that she could recognise them standing at the door. In cross-examination she stated that her husband went abroad but did not return and that there were 6 brothers and all were married except the 2 victims. She stated that there were 6 rooms in the place of occurrence house. She stated that in her room she and Gita Rani were there and before going to bed she closed the door. Pintu did not sleep in her room in that night and he was in his own room. Dilip and Pintu used to live in the same room. She stated that there was a varandha towards the west of the room running north and south with doors in the northern side. She stated that the dacoits entered into the southern room by breaking the door open and she was in the adjacent room of the victim Pintu. She stated that the victim was stabbed in her room and then her father-in-law opened the door of that room. She stated that being assaulted Dilip and Pintu entered into the room and that her father-in-law and mother-in-law were sleeping in the western barandah of that house. She stated that after the dacoits had left she found that ring, watch, money were taken away by the dacoits. She stated that out of fear she took shelter inside the room and she did not know the house of accused Musa @ Musaiya and she did know him earlier. She stated that his face was covered. She stated that she had seen accused Musa in the Jail and that in the Jail there were 2 lines of suspected persons and inside the Jail Musa was kept standing amongst them numbering about 150 in each line. She stated that witness one by one was taken inside the Jail and the accuseds were shown. She stated that her mother-in-law was the first person taken for recognition of the accused and she did not tell anything about recognition to her, then Gita Rani went inside and after coming back she disclosed that she had recognised accused Musa. She stated that accuseds were shown in the courtyard of the Jail and there were guards also and the Officer in-charge was also there She stated that she had told the Officer in-charge about recognition. She stated that police came on the following day at 4-00 PM. She denied a suggestion that her recognition of dacoits was false. She also denied a suggestion that she could not recognise the dacoits in the focus of torch light.

17. PW 4 Ledu Barua is the mother of the informant. She stated that dacoity took place at about 3-00 AM in the night following 19-4-85 in the house and in that night both the victims Dilip, Pintu and her husband, daughters-in-law Shanu, Gita Rani were in that house. She stated that there was scuffling between the dacoits and her sons Dilip and Pintu. She stated that Pintu caught hold of one of the dacoits and then a dacoit fired at her son Dilip who died at once and thereafter Pintu was given a dagger blow by the dacoits when he fell down and then the dacoits decamped with golden ring, wrist watch and cash of Taka 200.00 etc. She stated that she could recognise one dacoit Musa @ Musayia which was disclosed to one Nurul Islam. She stated that the dacoits were recognised in the focus of their torch light and she could recognise accused Nurul Islam @ Nurul Huq and she narrated about the same to the witnesses who came there. She also recognised Nurul Islam in the TI parade held inside the Jail. In cross-examination she stated that there was one varandha and 2 gudam ghars one of which had four rooms. She stated that her sons were in the middle of the said Ghar and her daughter-in-law Shanu was in the northern room and Gita Rani was in the middle room. She stated that she did not see the tussle between the dacoits and her sons. She stated that when she entered into the room from the varandha she found Dilip lying on the ground in the room of Cita and Pintu was in a standing position. She stated that she had not seen accused Musa and Nurul Islam before. She stated that she was kept inside Jail at the right side and there were many accused persons produced. She stated that the Daroga was with her. She denied that Daroga had showed her accused Nurul Islam. She stated that at the time of dacoity the face of Nurul Islam was not covered but there was a cap on his head. She stated that she could not recognise accused Musa at the time of dacoity.

18. PW 5 Gita Rani Barua is another bhabi of the informant who stated that her husband was not present at the time of occurrence. She stated that the dacoits entered into the house at about 3 a.m. following 19-4-85 i.e. 6th Baisakh. The dacoits after entering into the room started beating her brothers-in-law and one of the dacoits fired at victim Dilip and another gave stabbing blow in the abdomen of victim Pintu and that victim Dilip died instantaneously but Pintu died subsequently in the hospital. The dacoits took away golden ring, wrist watch and a sum of Taka 3000.00 and she had told the Daroga about recognition of the accused and she stated that she had recognised the accused in the TI parade held inside the jail by the Magistrate. She stated that at the time of dacoity 10/12 dacoits entered into the room and there were some other dacoits outside the room. In cross-examination she stated that her 2 brothers-in-law were in her room in the night. She denied a suggestion that she was giving false evidence being tutored.

19. PQ 6 is a Policeman who held Surat-hal on the dead-body of the victim Pintu Barua which was marked as Ext. 3 and his signature Ext. 3/1. He could not say whether he could see any sign of any injury on the body of victim Pintu.

20. PW 7 is a Constable who carried the dead body of victim Dilip to the morgue.

21. PWs 8 to 12 were simply tendered and they were not cross-examined by the defence.

22. PW 13 is the first investigation officer. He filled up the First Information Report form Ext. 5 with his signature as Ext. 5/1. He prepared the sketch-map and proved the same as Ext. 6 and his signature Ext. 6/1 and the index Ext. 7 and his signature thereon as Ext. 7/1 and he also proved the Explanatory Index as Ext. 8 and his signature thereon Ext. 8/1. He stated that he arrested some accuseds who confessed their guilt and thereafter he was transferred when he handed over the investigation to the subsequent investigation officer. He stated in cross-examination that the ejahar was received at the place of occurrence at 13.15 hours and same was recorded at the Thana at 21.45 hours and the distance of the place of occurrence from Thana was about 14 miles. He stated that GD Entry No. 614 dated 20-4-1985 was in connection of Case No. 3(4) 85 and when he reached Nazirhat in connection with an investigation he got the information about the dacoity and then he rushed to the place of occurrence. He stated that no TI parade was held and none of the accused made any statement while he was holding the investigation upto 5-7-85. On re-call he however proved some material Exts.

23. PW 14 is the Magistrate Mr. Tofazzal Ahmed who was the UNO at Fatikchari at the relevant time. He stated that he recorded the confessional statement of accused Ahammedul Huq and Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya on plain papers and that was best fitted at that time (with objection). He could not say when the accused persons were arrested. He stated that he recorded many confessional statements during his service period. He stated that it was not recorded in the statement sheet that the accused persons were given time for thinking or that they were making voluntary confessional. He of course stated in his deposition that the confessional statements were voluntary and true. He proved that confession of accused Ahammedul Haq as Ext. 9 and his signature as Ext. 9/1 and that of accused Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya as Ext. 9-Ka and his signature 9-Ka(1). He stated that in his order dated 30-10-85 it was written that Ahammedul Haq and Anowar Hossain were taken on police remand for 5 days and it was not written in the statement that there was no police at the time of recording the statements. It was also not written whether the accuseds would make any confession or not, they would not be sent back to the custody of the Police. He further stated that in 3 pages statement of accused Ahammadul Haq, his signature and that of accused Ahammadul Huq were in the last page and there was no signature of his own or of accused Ahmmadul Huq on the other 2 pages. He further stated that with 4 pages statement of accused Anowar, only in the last page there was a signature of accused Anowar and he admitted that he had no signature of his full name and it was also stated by him that there was no mention as to when he started the recording of confession and when he finished the same and he also did not give any certificate as to the involvement of the accused in the occurrence. He denied a suggestion that he did not follow the prescribed rules for recording a confession of an accused and the statement was not true and voluntary.

24. PW 15 Ahmed Hossain is another Magistrate of Fatikchari Upazila who held the TI parade of the suspected accused. He stated that on 24-11-85 he conducted the TI Parade inside the Chittagong Jail. He stated that the suspects were identified by the witnesses. Witness Ledu Bala Barua identified accused Nurul Islam @ Nurul Haq, witness Gita Rani Barua accused Md. Musa @ Musaiya @ Shapir Bap and witness Shanu Barua accused Musa (@ Musaiya @ Shapir Bap. He proved the TI parade report Ext. 10 and his signature Ext. 10/1. He stated that printed form for TI Parade was not available and he made the report on plain paper. In cross-examination he stated that there was permission to hold the TI. Parade on 14-11-85. He stated he could not tell when accused Nurul Islam and Musa were arrested and how many times they were taken to the court before TI parade. He stated that he fixed the date of TI parade. He also stated that TI. Parade report did not bear any seal showing his identity as a Magistrate and he did not also mention in his report that printed form was not available at that time. He denied a suggestion that he gave an opportunity to the witnesses to see accuseds after fixing the date for TI. Parade but before holding the same.

25. PW 17 is the last investigating officer. He took over the investigation of the case after 5-7-85 from the 1st investigating officer. He proved the Surat-hal reports as Exts. X and Y and the seizure-list Ext. 1.3. He stated that 4 of the accuseds were shown arrested and that accused Ahammadul Haq and Md. Anowar alias Bagiya made confessional statements before the Magistrate and that in the TI Parade accused Nurul Islam and accused Musa @ Musiya were recognised by witnesses. He stated that accused Musaiya was also implicated in Athajari PS Case No. 12 (7) 85. He also narrated that some of the accused were also involved in some other cases. He stated that he did not bring any record to show the names of the accused persons in those cases. He stated in cross-examination that on 2-9-85 he had shown Musa as arrested. He stated that the accuseds were taken on remand for 5 days and thereafter they were produced before the Magistrate on 30-10-85 for recording confession. He stated that the TI parade was held on 14-11-85. He stated that he was not present at the time of the TI Parade. He denied that at the time of remand he showed the accused to the witnesses and during remand the accused were severly tortured and thereafter the so-called confessional statements were recorded in the night at the residence of the Magistrate. He also denied a suggestion that in the TI parade he helped the witnesses to identify the accused persons and got the so-called TI Parade report from the Magistrate. He denied a suggestion that leaving out actual dacoits he falsely implicated these accuseds in this case. He denied a suggestion that the accuseds were not in any way connected with the occurrence.

26. Now, let us consider the first contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants including the condemned prisoner that the prosecution could not prove its case of dacoity with murder vis-a-vis place, time and the manner of occurrence by reliable and sufficient evidence. If we carefully consider the evidences of the PWs particularly of PWs 3-5 who are the inmates of the house of occurrence and most natural witnesses in this case, we find that they have in one voice stated that the occurrence took place at 3-00 in the night following 19-4-1985 and the dacoits entered into place of occurrence house by breaking the door and there was some scuffling in between the victims and the accused and then one of the dacoits fired at victim Dilip who at once fell down in the northern room of the house and died instantaneously. Thereafter another victim Pintu was stabbed with a dagger by another dacoit on his abdomen when he also fell down with bleeding injuries and he also subsequently died on the following day in the hospital where he was taken for treatment. The prosecution case as stated by the informant in the First Information Report has been sufficiently corroborated by some other PWs who witnessed the occurrence and some of whom came subsequently at the place of occurrence and saw the dead-body of victim Dilip and injured Pintu lying in the room of oocurrence and then injured Pintu was taken to the hospital for treatment but he subsequently died there. The police meanwhile came there and received the First Information Report and then held surat-hal on the dead body of victim Dilip which he found inside the northern room of the house and after the surat-hal the dead body was sent to the morgue for post mortem examination and report. Meanwhile the victim Pintu also died in the hospital. Then the Doctor PW 16 held post mortem examination on the dead bodies of both the victims namely Dilip and Pintu and gave the reports. From the post mortem reports it is quite clear that Dilip died of bullet injury and victim Pintu died of a stab injury which very well support the case of the prosecution. Thus it cannot be said that the occurrence did not take place at the time and the place as given by the prosecution. Of course, as to the manner of occurrence there are some discrepancies in the evidence of the PWs. Some of them namely PW 5 stated that the 2 victims were lying in the same room on the fateful night whereas PW 3 stated that there are 6 rooms in the house and that Pintu gave a blow on one of the accuseds and then Dilip was fired at by one of the dacoits but PW 5 did not say so. PWs 2, 3, 4 stated that out of 12/13 dacoits 4/5 entered into the room whereas PW 5 stated that 10/12 dacoits entered into the room and that there were some other dacoits outside the room. Further it is the case as made out in the ejahar lodged by the informant that the accused were wearing half pants, ganjis, lungis with malkocha and that the accused were aged between 15/20 years but PWs. 3-5 did not say anything as to the age of the accused and from the record it appears that accused Md. Anowar Bagaiya at the time of examination under section 342 CrPC was aged about 35 years and the accused Musa was aged about 50 years. So none of them was aged between 15/20 years as stated in the First Information Report. However from our careful consideration of the evidences as stated above, we are of the view that the prosecution has been able to prove the dacoity in the house of the father of the informant on the date, time and at the place as lodged in the First Information Report. Therefore we find no substance in the first contention of the learned Advocate for appellants.

<u>27. Now, the most important thing for us is to see how far these appellants are connected with the alleged dacoity and killing of the victims. As we have already pointed out that so far accused Md. Anowar Bagaiya is concerned there is no iota of evidence to prove that he is connected with the killing of the victims save and except his alleged confessional statement. But it has been forcefully contended by the Advocate for the appellants that the alleged confession Ext. 9-KA is in fact no confession in the eye of law and the same is also not admissible in view of the fact that it was not recorded in any regular form by the recording Magistrate after full compliance of the mandatory provisions of section 164(3) CrPC. For the scrutiny of the said confession of accused Anowar we may look into the Ext. 9-KA. Admittedly it has been recorded in a plain paper and from the evidence of PW 14 the learned Magistrate who recorded the same we find that he himself admitted that he did not assure the accused by saying that the accused would not be sent back to the Police custody whether he would make confession or not. It appears that the recording of Magistrate only put a few questions to the accused before the recording his alleged confession. For better appreciation and scrutiny of the confession we may quote the questions from the supplementary Paper Book as put to accused Anowar by the Magistrate as follows:</u>

<u>১) প্রঃ তোমার নাম ঠিকানা বল?</u>

<u>উঃ মোঃ আনোয়ার বাগাইয়া, পিং আব্দুল লতিফ, সাং কন্দলপুর থানা রাউজান।</u>

<u>(২) প্রঃ আমি কে আমাকে চিন?</u>

<u>উঃ চিনি আপনি হাকিম।</u>

<u>৩) প্রঃ তুমি পুলিশ বা কাহারো ভয়ে স্বীকার করিতেছ?</u>

<u>উঃ না, নিজ ইচ্ছায় জবানবন্দী দিতেছি।</u>

<u>৪) প্রঃ তোমার এই স্বীকারোক্তি তোমার বিরুদ্ধে স্বাক্ষী হইয়া দাড়াইতে পারে তা জান?</u>

<u>28. We have carefully examined this confessional vide Ext. 9-KA and we are of the view that the few questions put to the accused cannot be deemed to be sufficient to ascertain the truth and voluntariness of the alleged confession. It may be noticed that this particular confession appears to have been recorded just on the expiry of the period of remand of this accused Anowar when he was already in custody of the Police and suggestion was given during the cross-examination of the recording Magistrate that this confession was not true or voluntary and that during his remand he was severely tortured by the police to make the alleged confession.</u>

29. Now apart from the above matter fundamental legal requirement under section 164(3) CrPC has not been fulfilled in the so-called confession of the accused and that is a written memorandum to the confession by the recording Magistrate in specific form that is a mandatory provision, but in the so-called confession of the accused Anowar on the plain paper there is no such memorandum added to the confessional statement by the Magistrate and further from his evidence it appears that out of the 4-page confessional statement of the said accused, Magistrate's signature appears only on the last page without his seal or designation. In this connection the learned Advocate for the appellant has referred to a decision in the case of Jaheda Bewa and another vs. State reported in 5 BLD, 9 wherein the head note goes to the effect that, "Recording of confessional statement—Form of recording of the same-confessional statement of the accused recorded by Magistrate on a plain piece of paper and signed by the Magistrate at the bottom—Usual Form for recording confessional statement not used—Such confessional statement not admissible in evidence. Defect incurable even by subsequent examination of the recording Magistrate".

30. Another decision in the case of Abul Hossain and another vs. State reported in 46 DLR 77 has been referred to by the learned Advocate for the appellants. The last one was delivered by me in which detailed discussion has been made as to the requirements of recording confessional statement of an accused under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and it had been said that non-fulfillment of the requirements as outlined in the above decision will make the confession involuntary and unacceptable.

31. Keeping in view of the above principle already settled we have examined the instant confessional statement of accused Anowar and we are unable to accept the same as true and voluntary and the same bears no credibility to base conviction of the accused and it may be pointed out that a very materially defective so-called confessional statement appears to have been used against the alleged confessing accused Anowar Bagaiya and also against so-accused Musa @ Musaiya.

<u>32. Now, it will be found from the evidence of alleged eye-witnesses PWs 3-5 that there is no single word by the said witnesses as to who carried alleged gun to fire at the victim Dilip, They have made only allegations that the dacoits were armed with deadly weapons and they fired and stabbed the victims but none of these witnesses has said, that accused Musa carried any rifle or gun or he fired at the victim Dilip but the learned Additional Sessions Judge mainly relying upon the so-called confessional statement of co-accused Anowar B Bagaiya in which it was been stated that accused Musa opened fire during the occurrence, found that accused Musa was the killer of the victim Dilip by gun fire and awarded him the capital punishment of death. But law does not permit it. Even if it is found that the alleged confession is true and voluntary and genuine still the confession of a co-accused cannot be the sole basis of conviction of other co-accused which has been well settled in the case of Lutfun Nahar Begum vs. State reported in 27 DLR (AD) 29. Now, as there is no other evidence as regards the firing by rifle or gun, this so-called confessional statement of co-accused Anowar about firing by Musa by gun cannot be relied upon and used against him (Musa).</u>

33. The learned Deputy Attorney-General however submits that the questions put to the confessing accused were sufficient and the irregularities if any are curable under section 533 CrPC particularly when the recording Magistrate has been examined as a witness. He further stated that the memorandum if not appended to the confessional statement, at best it will be an irregularity which is curable and cannot vitiate the confession and make the same unacceptable. In his connection he has referred to a decision in the case of Hazrat famed vs. State reported in 11 DLR (SC) 84. The learned Advocate for the appellants however points out that the cited 11 DLR (SC) decision refers to a memorandum in respect of recording a statement under section 364 CrPC and not in a case of recording a confession under sub-section 3 of section 164 CrPC, hence the aforesaid decision of the Supreme Court is distinguishable and not applicable to the instant case and further the irregularity as detected in this case is not an irregularity but illegality which is not curable under section 533 of the Code of Criminal procedure as contended. In this connection decision in the case of Nurul Huq vs. State reported in 20 DLR 780 is cited by the learned Advocate for one appellant wherein it has been observed that—

"Any defect arising out of violation of any mandatory provision of law is not curable under section 533 CrPC."

34. We have heard the learned Advocates and perused the aforesaid decisions and we find substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants.

35. Now let us turn to the discussion of one of the most important points in this case relating to the recognition of the accused. Admittedly none of the witnesses could recognise the dacoits by name and none of them claimed to have known the dacoits since before and it is also an admitted fact that the night of occurrence was very dark as appears from the scrutiny of the Panjika of 1392 BS of Loknath Directory. It appears that 19th April 1985 i.e. the date of occurrence was the 6th Baisak 1392 BS. It was just one night before Amabashya because the following night was the night of Amabashaya and naturally at 3 A.M. in the night following 19-4-85, it was very dark and it is in the evidence of the PW 3 that when the dacoits entered into the room of the victim by breaking the door they at once, out of fear entered into the northern room of PW 3 and according to PW 3 she out of fear took shelter inside the room and the case of prosecution is that the accused could be seen by face in the focus of their torch lights. But in view of the prosecution case that out of fear PW 3 tried to hide herself for safety and that there was scuffling between the victims and the dacoits and at that moment one of the dacoits opened fire at victim Dilip who died at once and another dacoit stabbed victim Pintu with dagger who also fell down with profuse bleeding, how far it could be possible for the ladies PWs 3-5 to recognise the dacoits by face at that moment and further it is something unusual that the dacoits would focus their torch light on their own faces. Now, it is in the evidence of PW 3 that the inmates of the room could recognise only those accused whose faces were not covered by masks and according to her deposition accused Musa's face was covered by mask. If it was correct then how Musa could be recognised by face by the witnesses? It is in the evidence of PW 1 that he after hearing about the occurrence from the witnesses lodged the First Information Report in which he stated that the dacoits were found wearing half pants, Lungis with malkocha and their age was between 15-20 years but none of the witnesses in their depositions has stated that the accuseds were wearing half pants and they did not also mention a single word about the age of the dacoits, particularly about the ages of the accused appellants. In this context, we find it difficult to reply on the confessional statement of accused Anowar with implication of accused Musa in the commission of dacoity. It appears that for recognition of the accused a TI Parade was held. The order-sheet of the TI Parade has been brought before us through the supplementary paper-book in which we find that 8 suspects were placed for recognising by the witnesses in a TI parade held at the Chittagong Central Jail in presence of an Officer named Sultan Azizul Hoque who has not been examined in this case. Now, from the report we find, PW 4 Ledu Barua has recognised only accused Nurul Islam@ Nurul Hoque and PW 5 Gita Rani Barua has recognised accused Md. Musa @ Musaiya @ Shapir Bap and similarly PW 3 Shanu Barua has recognised the same Md. Musa @ Musaiya.

36. From this evidence of the 10 PW 15, we do not find anything as to how many under trial prisoners with 8 suspects of this case were mixed up for holding the TI parade whether the relevant provisions for the said purpose were complied with. In this connection first of all we like to refer to Regulation No. 282 of the Bengal Police Regulation 1943 at page 282 in Vol-1 wherein it has been stated inter alia that.

"The identification proceedings should be undertaken as soon as possible after the arrest of the suspected person or persons and care should be taken that before the commencement of the proceedings the identifying witnesses are kept in charge of a court peon or other person nor being a Police Officer at such a distance from the place where the proceedings are held as have no chance of seeing the suspects. The suspected person should, if possible be perused along with 8 or 10 persons, or if there are more than one suspect, with as many as 20 or 30 persons, similarly dressed and of the same religion and social status. Care should be taken that the mixing up of the suspect or suspects with the other persons does not take place in the view of the Police officers and the witnesses. Each identifying witness should then be brought singly in charge of the Magistrate's orderly or some other person, not being a police officer, to pick out the accused if he is able to do so. The identification by such witnesses should be conducted out of sight and hearing of other witnesses. If there is any fear that the identifying witnesses may be subjected to threats or inquiry should have become known to the suspects or to their friends, the witnesses should be allowed to view the persons paraded from a place where they themselves cannot be seen, as for instance through a window or an opening in a door or a wall. When the officer conducting the identification has satisfied himself that no communication between the police and the witnesses was possible, he should give a certificate to this effect."

37. Again it has been pointed out in the said provision that : "It should be borne in mind that the primary object of identification proceedings is to test the ability of the witness to identify a suspected person and to ascertain whether there is sufficient evidence to place him on trial. A Magistrate is chosen merely as a person whose impartiality and honesty is less likely to be called into question by the defence when the case is under trial."

38. It has been further stated in the said regulations that:

"Test identification shall, whenever circumstances, permit, be held inside the Jail. The above rules are applicable in the case of an under trial prisoner or a suspect in Jail. Men on bail shall not be mixed up with under trial prisoners except with the permission of the Magistrate."

<u>39. Now, in this connection the learned Advocate for the appellants has referred to a decision in the case of Anowar and another vs State reported in AIR 1961 Allahabad 50 as regards the requirements of holding a Test Identification Parade and assessment of evidence on identification of accused. The relevant portion may be quoted as follows:</u>

<u>"Although in assessing the evidence of identification it is neither possible nor desirable to lay down any hard and fast rules but certain guiding principles can be stated. One such principle the basic principle of Criminal law or the circumstances should be proved against the accused before it can be relied upon and used against an accused person. The evidence of identification is as much subject to the definition of the word 'proved' contained in section 3 (Evidence Act) and must satisfy the tests provided by that section. Prudence requires that the court should approach the evidence with reasonable doubt of an intelligent person and accept it only if those doubts are removed. The test excludes from its orbit blind faith of a true believer, because prudence and credulity do not go together" Para 18.</u>

<u>Now, the learned Advocate for the appellants has pointed out the other side of the TI Parade and made a grievance with regard to the identification of the appellants to the effect that identification parade in the instant case was a belated one and meanwhile the Police might have given chances to the witnesses to see the accused appellants and this unusual delay throws a doubt as to the genuineness of the identification of the accused appellants through the TI Parade. In this connection, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Soni vs. State of Uttar Pradesh reported in (1982) 3 (SC) Cases. 368(1), wherein it has been observed:</u>

<u>"It cannot be forgotten that the identification parade itself was held after a lapse of 42 days from the date of the arrest of the appellant. This delay in holding the identification parade throws a doubt on the genuineness thereof apart from the fact that it is difficult that after lapse of such a long time the witnesses would be remembering facial expressions of the appellant. If this evidence cannot be relied upon there is no other evidence which can sustain the conviction of the appellant".</u>

40. Now, keeping in view the above Police regulation and the decisions as cited before us if we examine the Test Identification Parade as held in this case we find that this accused Musa was shown arrested in this case on 2-9-85 though it is in the evidence of the I/O that he was arrested on that date but TI parade was held on 24-11-85 although an order for holding the TI Parade was made by court earlier. Now from 2-9-19-9 to 24-11-1985 it would be about 82 days i.e. about 3 months and it is not understood why the TI Parade was not held just after the arrest of the accused of the case particularly when it is the prosecution case that the witnesses would be able to recognise the dacoits if they were produced before them. PW 3 has stated that Gita Rani PW 5 was taken before her to identify the suspects and she identified accused Musa but after her coming back, she disclosed it to PW 3 but according to the prescribed rule, any way should be maintained and other formalities should be observed to ascertain the correct identity of the accused. PW 4 categorically stated that the accused were standing on the court yard of the Jail and the OC was also present there. Thus it appears that Police person was at the scene and as such the chance of false identification of the accused at the instance of the Police cannot be ruled out.

41. Mr. Chowdhury the learned Advocate for the appellants has also referred to a decision in the case of Nowsher Mollah and others vs. State reported in 11 BLD 295 wherein it has been observed that :

"Identification by torch light or hurricane light, at dead of night, is not sufficient unless the distance is a close proximity".

42. In the instant case the witnesses have come to say that they had recognised in the focus of the torch of the dacoits, of course in this case, no torch light has been recovered and admittedly the night was dark and in that situation how far the recognition of the dacoits could be possible by face by unknown persons is a matter to be taken into serious consideration. As against this about condemned prisoner Musa save and except this kind of recognition by witnesses PWs 3-5, there is no other evidence implicating him in the alleged dacoity or in leading the dacoits or firing at the victim Dilip. It appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has been influenced by the fact that there were some other cases pending against the accuseds of this case but unfortunately, he did not take notice of the fact that there was no paper to show that the accuseds were connected with the other cases but only as written in the charge-sheet. It may be pointed out that the prosecution must prove its case beyond all reasonable doubts by reliable and sufficient evidence and the onus of proof of the case is always on the prosecution and further even if some other cases are pending against the appellants for that he or they cannot be found guilty in this case unless this case is proved beyond all reasonable doubt by sufficient evidence. In any view of the matter, the prosecution in order to succeed must prove its case by sufficient and reliable evidence beyond all reasonable doubt. We cannot but hold that the confession is neither true nor voluntary and, as such, not acceptable and the same cannot be basis for conviction of accused Anowar and it also cannot lend any assurance to any other evidence to establish the charge against co-accused Musa, in view of the fact that against Musa except the so-called recognition, no other available evidence implicating him in-the dacoity has been brought on record.

43. Thus having considered all aspects of the case the evidences on record and its facts and circumstances we are of the view that the appellant Musa @ Musaiya and Anowar Bagaiya have been most illegally convicted and sentenced. The prosecution has failed to establish the complicity of the appellants in the alleged dacoity and killing of the victims by reliable and sufficient evidence and in that view of the matter their conviction and sentence are wholly bad and illegal and hence liable to be set aside.

44. In the result, the appeals of the appellants Musa @ Musaiya @ Shapir Bap, Jail Appeal No. 1407 of 1991 and Criminal Appeal No. 413 of 1991 are allowed, similarly the Criminal Appeal of Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya' being Criminal Appeal No. 826 of 1991 is also allowed and their convictions and sentences are set aside and accordingly the reference for confirmation of the sentence of death of the condemned prisoner Musa @ Musaiya @ Shafir Bap is rejected and they are acquitted of the charges brought against them.

Let appellant Md. Musa @ Musaiya Shapir Bap be immediately brought from the condemned cell to the jail custody and thereafter be set at liberty at once if not wanted in any other case. Let the appellant Md. Anowar @ Bagaiya also be set at liberty at once if not wanted in any other case. Send down the records.

End.
